hard_think: A complete inert byte generation is necessary but insufficient evidence for a runnable or securely activated Python process image.

The base-runtime projection must preserve executable, native extension, runtime library, runtime data, standard-library, and required directory topology while excluding site-packages and development surfaces.
Source immutability evidence and destination mutation authority are different capabilities and therefore require different lease access modes.
Activation, signing, empirical write denial, route ownership, A-grade, and retrieval-quality RSI remain later independently falsifiable gates.
dialectic_sweep: Copying the complete installed Python tree would include mutable dependencies and development material, collapsing base and dependency evidence roles.
Reusing dependency-runtime contracts would mislabel topology and omit Python executables, runtime libraries, Tcl data, and standard-library identity.
Granting DELETE access to a protected source is unnecessary authority; removing share denial would instead weaken source stability.
Calling this generation runnable or A-grade would convert a verified byte-copy result into an untested activation claim.
first_principles: A byte-closure generation must be content-addressed, complete, bounded, canonical, immutable after publication, and independently re-verifiable.
A query path remains read-only and cannot create, repair, activate, sign, route, or own runtime artifacts.
Every admitted file has one explicit role and every required role must be present; unknown files fail closed.
One validated layer is published before the next composition layer is authorized.

nonclaims: No base-runtime generation was activated or added to the live Holo route.

No Hermes execution, production worker dispatch, extension installation, or model authority was used.
